newsitem.title: CHINA: China development bank looking for foreign funds.
newsitem.headline: China development bank looking for foreign funds.

text.p: China's State Development Bank is exploring ways to raise foreign funds to finance major projects this year, the China Daily said on Monday.
The bank, which has won approval to issue $350 million worth of bonds in the United States, had not decided when it would make the issue, the newspaper quoted bank governor Yao Zhenyan as saying.
"We will select the appropriate time to issue international financial bonds this year," Yao said but gave no more details.
The bank needed to raise foreign capital to help finance ethylene plants, nuclear power plants and other large infrastructure projects, Yao said.
"The bank will take advantage of its high credit rating to raise foreign funds in overseas capital markets to assist the projects or enterprises," he said.

The bank would help support large and medium-sized projects by participating in international syndicated loans to borrow foreign exchange and by continuing to use export credits extended by foreign banks, Yao said.
The bank would grant loans to a water conservation project on the Yangtze river and a steel project in Panzhihua in southwestern Sichuan province, the newspaper said.
Bank officials were negotiating with foreign banks to raise $100 million to renovate an ethylene plant in Daqing in northeastern Heilongjiang province, it said.
The bank debuted on the international bond market last February when it issued 30 billion yen in samurai bonds.
